questions.question: Which of the following measures of money supply is most liquid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MI**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MI** is the most liquid measure of money supply.
 
• It includes currency in circulation, demand deposits at commercial banks, and other deposits that can be quickly converted to cash.
 
• MI is also referred to as narrow money because it focuses on the most liquid assets that are readily available for spending.
 
• Since MI encompasses the most immediately spendable forms of money, it is considered the most liquid measure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other measures of money supply include M2, M3, and M4, which add progressively less liquid assets.
 
• **M2** includes MI plus savings deposits, money market mutual funds, and other time deposits.
 
• **M3** includes M2 plus large time deposits, institutional money market funds, and other larger liquid assets.
 
• **M4** is the broadest measure and includes all of M3 plus other deposits.
 
• The liquidity of these measures decreases as the scope broadens from MI to M4.

questions.question: In which year was the Dandi March by Mahatma Gandhi launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1930**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi launched the **Dandi March **in the year **1930**.
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the **Salt March**, was a significant event in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was a nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly in colonial India.
 
• The march started on **March 12, 1930, and ended on April 6, 1930**, covering a distance of **240 miles** from **Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Dandi March was part of Gandhi's broader strategy of nonviolent resistance, known as Satyagraha.
 
• It drew worldwide attention to the Indian independence cause and inspired numerous movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
 
• The march marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement in India, which aimed at defying British laws and policies through nonviolent means.
 
• The Salt March is considered a pivotal event in the history of India's struggle for independence from British rule.

questions.question: Gangaur festival is historically native to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gangaur festival** is traditionally celebrated in the state of **Rajasthan**.
 
• It is one of the most important festivals in Rajasthan, observed in honor of Gauri, the wife of Lord Shiva, symbolizing marital bliss and conjugal happiness.
 
• Women, particularly those who are newly married, pray for the well-being of their husbands, while unmarried women pray for a good husband.
 
• The festival involves various rituals, including the making of clay idols of Gauri and Shiva, which are worshipped and later immersed in water bodies.
 
• Gangaur is celebrated with great enthusiasm and includes processions, traditional songs, and dances, making it a vibrant and colorful event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The festival of Gangaur is celebrated in the month of **Chaitra** (March-April), starting the day after Holi and continuing for 18 days.
 
• It is also observed in some parts of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, but it is most prominent in Rajasthan.
 
• Historically, the festival has been celebrated for centuries and is deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of Rajasthan.
 
• During the festival, women dress in their best attire and adorn themselves with jewelry.
 
• The festival strengthens the bonds of love and affection between married couples and within families.

questions.question: In India, Garibi Hatao and attainment of self - reliance was the main objective of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth Five Year Plan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fifth Five Year Plan** (1974-1979) of India aimed at **removing poverty (Garibi Hatao)** and achieving **self-reliance**.
 
• It was formulated and launched by the then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The plan focused on employment, poverty alleviation, and justice.
 
• It included programs such as the **Minimum Needs Programme** and the **Twenty Point Programme**.
 
• The plan was terminated in 1978 by the newly elected government, which introduced the **Rolling Plan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **First Five Year Plan** (1951-1956) focused on the primary sector, especially agriculture.
 
• The **Third Five Year Plan** (1961-1966) aimed at establishing a self-reliant economy and independent growth.
 
• The **Seventh Five Year Plan** (1985-1990) focused on rapid growth in food grains production, increased employment opportunities, and productivity.
 
• The Five Year Plans in India were centralized and integrated national economic programs aimed at achieving specific goals.
 
• The Planning Commission of India was responsible for formulating and implementing these plans until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

questions.question: Which of the following departments under the Ministry of Finance has launched the scheme "Vivad se Vishwas II" — (Contractual Disputes) to effectively settle the pending contractual disputes of government and government undertakings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Expenditure**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department of Expenditure** under the Ministry of Finance has launched the scheme "Vivad se Vishwas II" — (Contractual Disputes) to effectively settle the pending contractual disputes of government and government undertakings.
 
• The scheme aims to provide a faster and more efficient resolution mechanism for disputes, thereby reducing litigation and promoting ease of doing business.
 
• It is a part of the government's efforts to streamline processes and ensure timely completion of projects and contracts.
 
• The scheme is expected to benefit both the government and the contractors by reducing the time and costs associated with prolonged litigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Finance comprises several departments, including the Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Expenditure, Department of Financial Services, and Department of Revenue.
 
• The **Department of Expenditure** is responsible for overseeing the public financial management system in the Central Government and matters connected with state finances.
 
• It also oversees the implementation of recommendations made by the Finance Commission and the Central Pay Commission.
 
• The "Vivad se Vishwas II" scheme is an extension of the "Vivad se Vishwas I" scheme, which focused on resolving direct tax disputes.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with The Union and its Territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part I** of the Indian Constitution deals with "The Union and its Territories".
 
• This part consists of Articles 1 to 4.
 
• Article 1 declares India as a Union of States, and it also mentions the territories of India.
 
• Article 2 provides the power to admit into the Union or establish new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
 
• Article 3 deals with the formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing States.
 
• Article 4 provides for the laws made under Articles 2 and 3 to include supplemental, incidental, and consequential provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following five year plan of India was a complete failure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Five Year Plan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Five Year Plan** was implemented from 1961 to 1966.
 
• This plan aimed at making India self-reliant and self-generating in agricultural and industrial production.
 
• However, the plan was a **complete failure** due to several factors.
 
• It coincided with the Indo-China War (1962) and the Indo-Pakistan War (1965), which diverted resources and focus.
 
• Severe droughts in 1965 and 1966 further crippled the agricultural sector.
 
• As a result, the economy faced severe setbacks, and the plan did not meet its targets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **First Five Year Plan** (1951-1956) focused on agriculture and irrigation.
 
• The **Second Five Year Plan** (1956-1961) emphasized industrialization.
 
• The **Fourth Five Year Plan** (1969-1974) aimed at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
 
• The **Fifth Five Year Plan** (1974-1978) focused on removing poverty and achieving self-reliance.
 
• The **Seventh Five Year Plan** (1985-1990) aimed at accelerating food grain production, increasing employment, and raising productivity.

questions.question: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005. It promises ___________ days of guaranteed wage employment to all rural households in India who volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 days**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005 promises **100 days** of guaranteed wage employment to all rural households in India who volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• This act aims to enhance the livelihood security of people in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• The work provided under this scheme includes activities like water conservation, land development, afforestation, and rural connectivity among others.
 
• It is one of the largest work guarantee programs in the world and has been a key instrument in reducing rural poverty and unemployment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The act was notified on **5th September 2005** and was implemented in phases across India.
 
• This scheme is now known as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**.
 
• MGNREGA covers all districts of India except for those that have a hundred percent urban population.
 
• It also aims to create durable assets and strengthen the livelihood resource base of the rural poor.
 
• The scheme plays a crucial role in promoting inclusive growth by providing employment opportunities to the marginalized sections of society, including women, SC/STs, and other disadvantaged groups.

questions.question: H₂ is a Molecular Formula of which of the following elements ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen** is represented by the molecular formula **H₂**.
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe.
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, non-toxic, and highly combustible diatomic gas at standard temperature and pressure.
 
• Hydrogen is used in various applications including fuel cells, refining petroleum, and synthesizing ammonia for fertilizers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrogen** has an atomic number of 1 and is the first element on the periodic table.
 
• It is essential in the universe's chemical makeup, playing a key role in the formation of stars through nuclear fusion.
 
• Hydrogen has three main isotopes: Protium, Deuterium, and Tritium.
 
• In the industrial sector, hydrogen is primarily produced through natural gas reforming and electrolysis of water.
 
• It is considered a clean fuel as it produces only water when burned, making it a potential energy source for the future.

questions.question: Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) in Himachal Pradesh, 19,578 houses have been sanctioned in Himachal Pradesh and _________ houses have been completed as of November 9, 2023.

__
 
• **14,906 houses** have been completed under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) in Himachal Pradesh as of November 9, 2023.
 
• The scheme aims to provide affordable housing to the rural population by the year 2022.
 
• Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to the beneficiaries for the construction of houses.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's effort to achieve "Housing for All" by 2022.
 
• The scheme has specific criteria for the selection of beneficiaries, ensuring that the most deserving families receive aid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• It aims to construct 2.95 crore houses with all basic amenities by 2022.
 
• The financial assistance provided under the scheme is Rs. 1.20 lakh per unit in plains and Rs. 1.30 lakh per unit in hilly states, difficult areas, and Integrated Action Plan (IAP) districts.
 
• The houses built under this scheme are designed to be disaster-resilient and environmentally sustainable.
 
• The beneficiaries are selected based on the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data.

questions.question: A famous play, 'Abhijnana Shakuntalam' was written by which of the following personalities?

__
 
• **Kalidasa** was a renowned classical Sanskrit author.
 
• He is often considered the greatest poet and dramatist in the Sanskrit language.
 
• **'Abhijnana Shakuntalam'** is one of his most famous works, a play that tells the story of Shakuntala and King Dushyanta.
 
• This play is celebrated for its poetic excellence and has been translated into many languages worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kalidasa's other notable works include **'Meghaduta'** and **'Raghuvamsa'**.
 
• His works are marked by their exceptional literary quality and have had a lasting impact on Indian literature and drama.
 
• Kalidasa's contributions have made him a central figure in Indian cultural history, and his plays continue to be performed and studied widely.
